title: E-Books
text: Six open textbooks, free to read online. Written with bookdown and hosted on Rsquared Academy. Every title can also be downloaded as a PDF or ePub.

title: E-Books
text:
Learning path
The Core Track is designed to be followed end to end. The two companions slot in alongside it rather than after it.


Core 01

Intro to R

BeginnerZero to running code. RStudio, packages, help.




Core 02

Data Wrangling

BeginnerImport, reshape, dplyr, pipes, tibbles.




Core 03

Viz with ggplot2

IntermediateGrammar of graphics through to publication polish.




Core 04

R, Databases & SQL

IntermediateDBI, dbplyr, queries, joins.

Shortcut: already wrangling data in SQL? Take 04 straight after 02.





Companion A — Foundational Tooling

Command Line Basics

BeginnerFiles, permissions, pipes and scripting for R users. Pair with Core 01.


On Windows: everything works from the RStudio Terminal, Git Bash or WSL — chapter 1 covers all three.




Companion B — Graphics Deep-Dive

Data Viz with Base R

IntermediateBase graphics engine, parameters, multi-panel layouts, production export. Zero dependencies. After Core 03.

title: R Packages
text:
Ten packages, all on CRAN, all documented, all actively maintained. Each was written while teaching at Rsquared Academy and shared in the hope that others find them useful.
The goal is software which is user friendly, light weight, well tested and well documented. Major bugs get fixed quickly; feature requests are considered but not promised.
Full descriptions and vignettes: pkgs.rsquaredacademy.com.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
I build statistical software that holds up outside a tutorial, and I help teams do the same. My work sits where R, statistics, economics and finance overlap — regression diagnostics, customer segmentation, descriptive and inferential statistics, and the unglamorous plumbing that keeps an analysis reproducible six months later when someone else has to rerun it.
Most of that work is open source. The package portfolio below is used far more widely than I expected when I started writing it, and it is the reason people find their way here: the packages are free, the vignettes are free, and there is no upsell attached to any of it.
I also write. Six data science textbooks are free to read online, and I founded Rsquared Academy, an open-source education platform for data science, where the courses behind those books live.
I earned my postgraduate degree from Madras School of Economics (Anna University), Chennai, and now maintain the portfolio independently from Bengaluru, India.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Teaching
I run Rsquared Academy, where the courses behind the books are taught in full. It is an open-source education platform, not a lead-generation funnel — the course material is written to be useful even if you never sign up for anything.

For individuals. Self-paced and live courses on R, the tidyverse, visualization, SQL and command-line tooling.
For teams. Masterclasses built around your own data and problems, run as hands-on sessions rather than lectures.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Consulting & Advisory
Custom package development and architecture. Internal R or Python tooling built to survive handover: documented, tested, and structured so your team can extend it without me. Most consulting work is undocumented code that one person understands, and that is a single point of failure I can help remove.
Team masterclasses. Tidyverse, SQL, command-line tooling. Built around your data, your conventions and your team’s existing stack.
Who this is for: teams shipping quantitative work that other people have to maintain. Who it is not for: one-off analyses, or anyone looking for a pre-packaged answer.

Schedule an intro call

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Everything in one app
xplorerr bundles the whole set behind a single install, and adds a visualizer the other packages do not have. If you are not attached to a particular package, start here.




Docs CRAN GitHub



xplorerr

All seven apps

Descriptive, inferential, visual, RFM, linear and logistic — one package, one install.


Seven launchers. Each opens its own app window.

install.packages("xplorerr")
xplorerr::app_linear_regression()   # linear
xplorerr::app_logistic_regression() # logistic
xplorerr::app_descriptive()         # descriptive
xplorerr::app_inference()           # inference
xplorerr::app_vistributions()       # distributions
xplorerr::app_rfm_analysis()        # segmentation
xplorerr::app_visualizer()          # visualizer

title: Interactive Apps
text:
Which launcher should I use?
Both routes work and reach the same apps. The difference is who owns them.



Option A

One install, seven apps

Install xplorerr and call any app_*() function. Nothing else to install.


Best if you want the visualizer, or several apps at once.






Option B

The owning package

Install the package that owns the app and call its own launcher.


Best if you already use that package for its non-interactive functions.


Package reference











nse2r has no app here



nse2r did ship a Shiny app for NSE market data, but the package was archived on CRAN on 2023-08-07 and is under revival, so it gets no app card. Nothing to install and nothing to link to.

title: Privacy
text:
This page says exactly what happens when you visit this site, including the parts that are less convenient to read. It is written to be short and specific rather than comprehensive, because a policy nobody finishes is not a policy.
Last reviewed: 7 October 2026.

title: Privacy
text:
The short version

The site is a static set of pages hosted by Netlify. There is no server-side code, no database, no account, and nothing to sign up for.
It sets no cookies and runs no advertising or remarketing tags.
Two things are loaded from other companies’ servers: Google Analytics, but only after you agree to it, and Google Fonts, which happens automatically before you are asked. Both are described below, and the font one is called out honestly rather than buried.
Nothing you type here reaches me. There is no form on this site.

title: Privacy
text:
Who runs this site
Aravind Hebbali, based in Bengaluru, India. The contact address is the same one in the footer of every page. If anything on this page is wrong or unclear, that is worth telling me about.

Google Fonts is the awkward one, and it is worth being direct about: the Bootstrap theme this site uses includes a stylesheet rule that pulls the font from fonts.googleapis.com. That request reaches Google before the consent banner is answered, and it necessarily discloses your IP address to them in the process. Self-hosting the font would remove it; that change is worth making and I have not made it here.
The rest of the site has no third-party embeds at all — no videos, no maps, no chat widgets, no social media buttons that load anything. Calendly and LinkedIn appear only as ordinary links that take you to another site, and those sites have their own policies.

title: Privacy
text:
Google Analytics
Used for one purpose: knowing which pages get read. It is configured for basic page measurement, with no advertising or conversion features.
If you accept, a page view sends Google the page you are on and its title, the page you came from, your approximate country and city derived from your IP address, your browser, operating system, screen resolution and language, and an identifier stored in a cookie so your visits can be grouped. The IP address itself is used to work out the location and is not stored. Google’s own documentation on what Google Analytics collects and how location works covers this in more detail than a site policy can.
Two things you should know that are easy to miss:

Google Signals is switched on for this property, which lets Google report aggregated demographic and interest data. Google states this data is not used to identify individual visitors, but the setting lives in the Analytics property rather than on this site, and it was on when I looked.
There is no advertising measurement. No Google Ads tag is present, so no click identifiers are sent and your visits here are not connected to any ad profile I control.

If you choose “essential only”, the tag still loads so I can see that a page was viewed, but with storage denied. You get an anonymous page count and no cookie is set.

title: Privacy
text:
Links to other sites
This site links to package documentation on CRAN and Rsquared Academy, book downloads, GitHub repositories, LinkedIn, Calendly, and a blog. Those are plain links: nothing is loaded from them until you click, and once you do, their own privacy policies apply rather than this one.

title: Privacy
section: What this site does not do
text:
What this site does not do
No advertising. No remarketing or retargeting. No selling or sharing of data. No behavioural profiling for ads. No third-party analytics other than the one above. No cross-site tracking of any kind. No server logs containing personal data beyond what Netlify records automatically for delivering files.

title: Privacy
text:
Contact
Questions, corrections, or a request to delete data associated with your visits — email me at the address in the footer. Requests about the data Google Analytics holds are best made directly to Google, which is the only party that can act on them; I can only stop sending new data.
